in writing. the report on the updating of the legal framework for european statistics on permanent crops, which i voted in favour of, is moving in the right direction as it adapts to the current needs of users and the market. reducing the administrative burden and simplifying the questionnaires will allow more complete data to be collected on the volume of production, products and their cultivation on the european market. the collection of reliable data has a two-fold positive effect, on the one hand helping to make good decisions on demand, production and diversification of european agricultural products to make them more competitive and on the other informing farmers and agricultural cooperatives on how to make the best use of their land. in fact, for greece, a country with a rather strong presence of the primary sector in the economy, improving these statistics is useful.
in writing. i voted in favour of mrs nedelcheva's report on the use of statistics on permanent crops, as i believe that they constitute a reliable basis for taking sound decisions on agricultural production and the european market. i agree with the rapporteur on the need to reduce the administrative burden associated with the production of statistics and with her amendments to the proposal for a regulation.
in writing. i voted against the report, as well as the other two related reports (březina a7-0340/2011 and březina a7-0358/2011) because not only are no solutions being promoted towards the abolition of nuclear energy, but, on the contrary, the use of nuclear energy and the funding of related research are being promoted. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. the main reason for the negative vote is based on the firm and overall position against nuclear weapons. unfortunately, the report reproduces the distorted view of the usefulness of nuclear energy for economic reasons and to combat climate change. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of radioactive waste. it also promotes the need for the union to 'lead the way' in this area. on the contrary, the appropriate financing, particularly in the present crisis, is that of sustainable and renewable development which is genuinely compatible with environmental and social needs.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on a new consumer strategy because i think it is moving in the right direction for consumer protection. the importance of informing consumers of their rights and of safeguarding food safety is emphasised. i agree with the rapporteur that there is a need for better consumer protection in the financial services and food sectors, as we spend a large part of our income on food. the consumer agenda is a key tool for consumer protection and for meeting the objectives of the eu 2020 strategy.
in writing. the economic importance of online gambling is constantly growing, covering almost half of the total betting market. member states are solely responsible for the legislation surrounding the sector. it is positive that the eu recognises the specific nature of this market in view of the risks it entails in relation to consumer protection and the fight against organised crime. the creutzmann report proposes a number of effective measures to eliminate illegal supply and to strengthen consumer protection. despite the positive provisions of the report, i voted against it as it leaves open the possibility of deregulating/liberalising the online gambling market. this not only effectively cancels out the above proposals but also increases the opportunities for illegal practices such as match-fixing, illegal betting cartels, money laundering, underage betting, etc.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report, but i differed in paragraph 44 in favour of the proposal on the financing of social projects through lotteries. the market for electronic games is one of the largest in the eu. it is noted that there are currently around 15000 gambling websites operating. over 85% of them are unlicensed and the annual turnover of this market is estimated at eur 10 billion. the commission has also proposed that the commission should be given the task of drawing up a report on the application of the competition rules to the market in electronic money. the fragmentation of its rules of operation according to the national priorities of each member state thus creates different legal frameworks and divergent and often contradictory policies. and a market governed by complex and fragmented rules is a market prone to financial crime and fraud. the recent experience of match-fixing proves it. the report is therefore moving in the right direction, stressing that match-fixing and any action which offends sport can and must be tackled more effectively at european level.
in writing. the ep report on bee health and beekeeping, while noting the decline in bee colonies and the effects on pollination, the need to control bee diseases and the general monitoring of bee health, does not, however, prohibit the use of pesticides for which there are direct reports of adverse effects on bee health. it does not oppose the prohibition of the cultivation of genetically modified organisms either for human consumption or for animal feed. the common agricultural policy is based on the principle of safeguarding the profits of the large business groups operating in this sector. the lack of drugs to combat bee diseases cited in the report is due to the fact that in a capitalist economy companies cannot be forced to do research in areas where there is not much profit. this contradiction can only be resolved by the socialisation of the basic means of production and central planning of the economy, with popular power that will exploit both agricultural and livestock production and research for the people's welfare.
in writing. the simon report is based on the commission's proposal for the forthcoming revision of the state aid package for services of general economic interest. these services are considered to be of particular importance to all citizens, but without state intervention they would be provided inadequately or not at all. the report presents the overall objective of the reform as being to enhance the contribution that sgeis can make to the wider european economic recovery. it also rightly states that citizens need high-quality public services, and in particular social services that mitigate the social impact of the crisis. unfortunately, while the report successfully recognises the importance of the public service for citizens, the guidelines it gives for its operation fall within the framework of the anti-social eu2020 strategy. in this way, the operation and financing of the sgeis are to the maximum extent determined by the provisions on non-distortion of competition and their role is clearly undermined. i therefore voted against this report.
in writing. i voted in favour of mr simon's report because i believe that services of general interest not only play a decisive role for individual citizens, but are also of enormous importance for the well-being of society as a whole. these are services which the state or the state authorities consider to be of particular importance to all citizens. these services make a significant contribution to economic efficiency and competitiveness and enhance social, economic and territorial cohesion in the eu. it is important, however, to provide guarantees for the correct application of the rules so that these undertakings, which are entrusted with the provision of public services, are able to fully implement the tasks assigned to them.
in writing. the economic crisis affecting many member states is not only preventing the reduction of poverty and social exclusion but is, on the contrary, leading to a worrying deterioration. it is significant that the eu, although one of the richest regions in the world, has more than 80 million people at risk of poverty, 30% of whom are children. in countries particularly affected by the crisis, such as greece, poverty threatens one third of the population when the community average is well below. the report, which i voted in favour of, recognises that under the current circumstances europe, despite its commitments, will not be able to meet its strategic target of reducing the number of citizens at risk of poverty by 20 million by 2020. it therefore calls on the commission to increase and better target the funding of programmes aimed at combating poverty and on the member states, which is also an important issue for greece, to strengthen social health, care and education services to bridge the skills gap, promote social inclusion of individuals and combat poverty and social exclusion.

acting president of the council. - madam president, the house! i have the honour, as the representative of the polish presidency, to present the position of the european union and the member states on world aids day, as agreed with the european commission and subsequently adopted by the council on 28 november 2011. today, on world aids day 2011, the european union and its member states join people around the world in honouring the memory of their relatives, friends and loved ones who have died of aids and reaffirm their commitment to supporting all people living with hiv and affected by the aids epidemic. this year marks a special anniversary: exactly 30 years ago, the world learned about hiv and aids. the first cases of aids were identified in december 1981. during these 30 years of struggle and sacrifice of millions of people, over 30 million people have lost their lives and 16 million children have been orphaned by aids. hiv and aids have affected every country, every community and every family. an estimated 33.3 million people worldwide are currently living with hiv, and 7,000 new infections occur every day, mostly in low- and middle-income countries. the last 30 years have also been a period of unprecedented commitment and partnership. in the face of hiv, we have learned the value of partnership and dialogue, and we have learned that human rights and human dignity should always be at the forefront. impressive progress has led to a nearly 20% decline in new hiv infections globally over the past decade and a nearly 19% decline in aids-related deaths between 2004 and 2009. the greatest progress has been made in the most affected region, sub-saharan africa, where two-thirds of all people living with hiv live. the european union is proud that its efforts, together with such important partners as unaids, who, the global fund to fight aids, tuberculosis and malaria, unitaid, people living with hiv and civil society, have contributed to remarkable achievements in the global fight against hiv and aids. in 2010, the european union's contribution to the global fund to fight aids, tuberculosis and malaria was close to usd 1.5 billion, representing 53% of the total contributions to the fund (the european commission and member states together). however, more than 8 million people in low- and middle-income countries still need access to effective treatment, and the number of new infections still exceeds the number of people starting treatment. this means that hiv and aids continue to be one of the biggest obstacles to these countries' progress. in seven countries, including five in eastern europe and central asia, hiv infections increased by more than 25% between 2001 and 2009. through partnerships with these countries, the eu has stepped up its efforts to change this unacceptable situation, calling for an urgent intensification of prevention programmes and services at regional and national level that can lead to the elimination of hiv and aids. the european union will play a decisive role in the fight against hiv and aids by strengthening its leadership and better adapting the action of the european union institutions to the changing hiv context at global and european level. the challenge for us now is to keep aids as a priority and to accelerate action at the global, regional, national and local levels to end the epidemic. the european union welcomes the comprehensive review of progress made towards the commitments under all the millennium development goals of 2000 and the ambitious targets for 2015 set out in the political declaration on hiv/aids, entitled 'increasing efforts to eliminate hiv/aids', adopted at the united nations general assembly high-level meeting on aids in june 2011. achieving these goals will bring us closer to a world without new hiv infections, aids-related deaths and discrimination. the european union joins the community of people fighting the aids epidemic in supporting the unaids strategy of zero new infections, zero discrimination and zero deaths from hiv/aids getting to zero and, on the occasion of world aids day, reaffirms its commitment to our common task of ending the hiv epidemic. we reaffirm the european union's commitment to working towards the 2015 targets of initiating antiretroviral treatment for 15 million people living with hiv, halving the number of sexually transmitted infections, halving the number of hiv infections among people who inject drugs, eliminating mother-to-child transmission of hiv and significantly reducing maternal deaths from aids. the european union stresses that prevention is the most effective way to stop the hiv epidemic. we need to ensure that prevention strategies are comprehensive, are developed on the basis of available knowledge with full respect for human rights and understanding of the local context, while making the fullest use of prevention methods already in place and promoting new methods and technologies. the european union is concerned that women and girls are particularly vulnerable to hiv infection due to physiological, economic and social factors, gender inequalities and violence. women and girls account for more than 50% of all people living with hiv, and hiv and aids remain the leading cause of morbidity and mortality among women of reproductive age. the european union will therefore step up its efforts to promote a gender-sensitive approach, equal rights and the empowerment of women, and to promote women's rights, in particular the right to protection against risky sexual behaviour, especially in the context of combating trafficking in human beings and all forms of sexual exploitation. at the same time, attention should be paid to promoting responsible behaviour, especially among men. the european union pays particular attention to populations at the highest risk of infection, including men who have sex with men, people who inject drugs, migrants, prisoners, ethnic minorities, sex workers and their clients. these populations are often marginalised and difficult to access, making them more vulnerable to hiv infection. at the same time, we note with concern that most young people still have limited access to sexual and reproductive health programmes that offer information, skills, services and social support. it is of the utmost importance to ensure wide access to specifically designed prevention programmes and services, including confidential hiv testing and counselling, high quality and affordable male and female condoms, comprehensive sexuality education, harm reduction programmes and other available prevention measures. when planning effective hiv prevention and care, the prevention and treatment of other sexually transmitted infections, such as hepatitis b and c and tuberculosis, should be considered. we call for deeper cooperation in this area and for the integration of hiv and aids programmes into primary health care, including sexual and reproductive health programmes, and for the strengthening of programmes and services related to the prevention and treatment of all these diseases. the european union recognises the need for greater involvement of people living with hiv or aids in all aspects of the planning, implementation and monitoring of prevention and support policies, strategies and programmes. we recognise the crucial role of ngos, including those that bring together people and communities affected by hiv, in supporting national and local action in this area. the european union welcomes the significant increase in the availability of antiretroviral treatment, but notes with concern the variation in availability across regions. more than 6.5 million people in low- and middle-income countries are currently receiving antiretroviral treatment. but there are still eight million people who are eligible for treatment who are not. recent scientific findings on the efficacy of antiretroviral medicines increase the potential for hiv prevention and the fight against the epidemic. we would like to underline our commitment to universal access to antiretroviral treatment, care and support for people living with hiv or aids and the importance of national engagement and investment, with due regard for the dignity, rights and freedoms of people affected. the european union welcomes the significant decrease in the number of new hiv infections transmitted from mother to child. we reaffirm our commitment to action leading to universal access to vertical infection prevention to eliminate hiv infection among children and save the lives of their mothers. the european union reaffirms that all people living with hiv or aids, in particular children and young people, should have access to the best available care, treatment and support. we reiterate the need to integrate hiv/aids and sexual and reproductive health and rights into strategies and programmes at local, national, regional and international levels. member states should protect persons living with hiv or aids from discrimination, stigmatisation and deprivation of their rights and freedoms. the european union also reaffirms its commitment and support for the abolition of restrictions on the right of entry and short- and long-term residence of persons living with hiv, the decriminalisation of homosexuality and the abolition of its laws, as such legal provisions are neither adequate tools to combat the epidemic nor provide support to populations at particular risk of infection. the european union recognises that in times of economic crisis, the appropriate allocation of available resources, including for health promotion and prevention, is a key issue. we therefore reaffirm our strong commitment to work towards the effectiveness and efficiency of existing programmes and services and to strengthen national health systems and human resources necessary to provide the health, education and social services essential for the prevention, treatment, care and support of people living with hiv/aids. only by continuing our work, by stepping up high-quality and effective action and by closing the existing gaps in all areas, will the european union as a whole and each of its member states be able to make a significant contribution to reducing new infections, stigma and discrimination and aids-related deaths.
member of the commission. − i thank all those who took part in this debate for the strong message they are giving to continue our fight against the hiv/aids disease. this strong message is all the more important today when, due to the austerity programmes we are having in europe, much of the resources that were being allocated to the health sector are being reduced. it is important that our message today is that cost reductions in our countries' budgets must be achieved by fighting waste and not by cutting funding programmes such as for hiv/aids and by the stronger investment we need in prevention. over the past few years substantial progress has been made in our fight against this disease. but we are still far from reaching our target of zero new infections, aids deaths and discrimination. but, and here i can give the commission's full commitment, it is our commitment to continue to work tirelessly to achieve these objectives. we need to ensure that we fight discrimination, which is a major scourge in many european countries, and that we ensure access to care for all those infected or at risk of infection with this disease both in europe and outside europe. but as some of you have said, we also need a strong effort in educating our people, our citizens, on everything that has to do with hiv/aids infection. i make sure we continue our work. on the commission side we have run a platform, the so-called anti-aids/hiv 'think tank' which is made up of member states where we try to push as far as we can to have best practices in all our member [countries] so that our action is coordinated and then we can expect better results.

in writing. in 2009, the rate of early school leaving for all young people aged 18 to 24 in europe stood at 14,4% when the member states themselves have committed to reducing this rate to 10% by 2020. greece has one of the highest rates of early school leavers after primary education and almost the highest rate of early school leavers among young immigrants (over 40%). the social and economic implications are significant. they range from the social marginalization of early school leavers and fewer job opportunities to the reduction of a country's economic potential. it is estimated that reducing the rate of early school leavers across europe by just 1% would increase the number of skilled young people by half a million each year, with a corresponding contribution to the gdp of these countries. the report, which i voted in favour of, underlines these consequences, while proposing a series of actions, such as reform of the education system, extension of the institution of 'second chance' and strengthening of the community resources earmarked for this purpose.

mr president, perhaps nothing betrays more the degree of homogeneity of a state or supranational entity than the consistency of the way it treats those it perceives as third parties. historically, many confederations of autonomous states came very close when they adopted policies of uniform treatment of the presence of nationals of other states on their territory. the uniform policy of the various states in dealing with foreign nationals is a common and often cited example of immigration policy. today we are again debating a draft directive which, despite its initial reservations, goes one step further by providing for common rules on the treatment of third-country nationals residing in the territory of the european union, and the role of the rapporteur, mrs mathieu, whom i thank in turn, in overcoming the differences is a given and a reality and i cannot understand why the socialist group ultimately abstained from voting in the libe committee. the direct benefits of this directive are obvious: less red tape, greater legal certainty in the schengen area, building trust between member states, more effective fight against irregular immigration, common rules on the labour assessment of third-country nationals' professional qualifications, benefits for social security and health care. and the benefits in the medium term are even greater. the fact that the third country national is treated in the same way in greece, the netherlands, sweden and every other member state of the union is another step towards a unified approach to our common future. i therefore think that the adoption of this directive is an important step for the legislator, for the european parliament, a major step towards the adoption of a common european immigration policy and, ultimately, another important step on the road to european integration.

vice-president of the commission. − madam president, i should like to thank the members for a very serious and substantive debate and for their support for this regulation and for the commission’s actions in this regard. concerning the question posed by ms bowles on the literature behind this scoreboard, the commission is currently working on background papers that will explain the economic rationale underlying the choice of indicators, including the relevant economic literature and the determination of thresholds. i can commit myself, the commission, and even dg ecfin to providing you with these background papers concerning the underlying economic rationale. ms podimata referred to a certain british financial media source. i do not think its words are sacrosanct. i recall, for instance, that in that source the euro area was not described as a small open economy, but i have a feeling that some commentators consider that the euro area is a large, closed economy. it is not a large closed economy. instead it is a large open economy that trades a very large share of its gdp with the rest of the world. this has obvious implications for the construction of our analytical mechanism of macroeconomic imbalances. the legislation enshrines the approach of intelligent symmetry, whereby surveillance covers both deficits and surpluses, but clearly underlines that there is greater urgency in tackling large deficits. moreover, policy responses need to be differentiated. i refer to the alert mechanism report which, in article 3.2, states ‘the assessment of member states showing large current account deficits may differ from that of member states that accumulate large current account surpluses’. i think the background noise suggests that it is time to close this debate. it is not very conducive to analytical debate on macroeconomic imbalances, so i suggest we continue our dialogue in the committee on economic and monetary affairs shortly.

member of the commission. − madam president, thank you very much for this lively discussion. i would like to start my answer by saying that, for the countries that joined the european union in 2007, the same transitional arrangements apply as for the intake of 2004, and the same arrangements also apply to croatia, for which the agreement was recently signed. this also allows us to look at the experience of the 2004 group by way of comparison. this i believe strongly supports the argument that the receiving countries hugely benefited from mobile workers from new member states, and also the united kingdom, on which there has been an exchange of views in the debate. i think it is very important to say that, despite the fact that the actual number of workers coming from poland and other countries was much higher than originally expected, we have to stress the enormous economic benefit of this contribution as opposed to speaking about these mobile workers being a burden on social security or the health care system. i think it is very useful to look at the debates in germany and austria, in which i participated in the spring period of this year, before 1 may, when these two countries also eventually had to open up their labour markets for the 2004 intake. there was clearly a feeling that these two countries probably lost out by maintaining the restrictions until the last possible day, and that perhaps it would have been much wiser for them to have opened up earlier, especially because of the specific demographic conditions of germany and also the very good labour market performance of the large number of vacancies this country has. i think this should be a lesson and an example for others. in the current situation, i think we have to look at the concrete labour market conditions in each and every country and not only the european average. as we all know, the european averages are not very encouraging. we have been stuck with a very high unemployment rate – about 10% – and the coming year is not expected to be very easy. however, this average masks very great discrepancies, and this is why i would agree with those who suggest that, in countries where the unemployment rate is very low, like austria or the netherlands, it will be very difficult to provide factual justification for the maintenance of these restrictions. i also have to stress that some members of the house rightly pointed to the very complex and sometimes (unfortunately) xenophobic discussions in the netherlands vis-à-vis mobile worker citizens from other eu member states. such discourse definitely does not help a constructive solution or response to this question to emerge. it is very clear that the economies of some of these countries we are speaking about need more workers, also from other eu countries. the business community is expressing this opinion, and i think wise policy-makers will pay attention to this. we have been engaged with the governments of these countries: i have written letters to all of them and explained what the rules are and what we expect. i can tell you that we have so far received only one notification or request from member states about the extension of the restrictions. previous experience has shown that member states tend to wait until the very end of the period to send their notifications, and so far only the united kingdom has sent one, on 24 november. this notification states that the uk decided to retain labour market restrictions following the advice from the independent migration advisory committee, which stated in its report of 4 november 2011 that, based on an analysis of recent labour market indicators, the uk labour market is in a state of serious disturbance and that removing existing restrictions would increase the risk of an increased inflow of eu2 nationals, with a potential negative impact on the uk labour market. as we know from new statistics, unemployment in the uk is at a 17-year high, but i think it has to be stressed that foreign workers should not be blamed for this. we have to look at the situation in the case of the uk and, should others come, on a case-by-case basis. the commission will check at the beginning of next year whether the member states that have a right in this context have provided, together with the notification, an explanation – with supporting evidence and pertinent arguments – on the existence of a serious labour market disturbance or threat thereof. if a member state has, for example, not provided an explanation at all or has not provided an explanation with sufficient data and pertinent arguments, the commission will ask the member state to provide the missing information. the commission services will examine the notification and the explanations and the data provided by the member states. i am planning to present my summary to the ministers in the epsco council in february.

the next item is the report by mr jens geier, on behalf of the committee on budgetary control, on the budgetary control of eu financial assistance to afghanistan (2011/2014 (ini)) (a7-0388/2011)
the debate is closed. the vote will take place on thursday 15 december 2011 at 11.30. written declarations (rule 149) the president of the court of justice shall be informed of the decision of the court of first instance.
in writing. i would like to congratulate the rapporteur on his excellent report on such an interesting and vital subject as the budgetary control of eu financial assistance to afghanistan. our role and duty as the european parliament is to respect the principle of sound financial management of the financial support granted by the eu through the community budget, that is, through the money of the european taxpayers. compliance with this principle should apply to aid granted in the member states of the union as well as in third countries. in this spirit, i warmly support the rapporteur's call on the european commission to correct the weaknesses identified in the audit work by the european court of auditors and third party audit bodies. accountability should also be strengthened with regard to eu funds channelled to afghanistan and managed by certain un agencies, as eu institutions should have access to the internal reports of these agencies. through transparency and accountability we can ensure that the money of the union budget is spent correctly and efficiently.
the next item is the report by nicole kill-nielsen, on behalf of the committee on foreign affairs, on the eu strategy for central asia (2011/2008 (ini)) (a7-0338/2011)
member of the commission. − madam president, i welcome the european parliament draft resolution on the implementation of the eu strategy for central asia. it is a timely contribution for the review of the strategy which will be undertaken over the coming year. central asia is a region of growing importance to the european union. the region borders afghanistan and faces security threats with implications for the eu. these implications include terrorism, drug trafficking and other cross-border crime. widespread poverty in some countries and incomplete political and economic reform processes pose challenges, not only for the countries themselves, but also for regional cooperation and security. at the same time the region is rich in resources and has the potential of diversifying energy export routes to the eu and contributing to eu energy security. there is significant interest among the countries in the region to strengthen relations with the eu. since the adoption of the strategy on central asia by the european council in 2007, the eu has managed with limited resources and within a relatively short time to significantly increase its role in central asia. our key role in close cooperation with the osce and the un in helping the kyrgyz republic to overcome its crisis last year and supporting the development of a parliamentary democracy there is a good example of the importance of our increased engagement. the strategy on central asia has led to other important developments worth noting. we have established regular high-level political dialogue between the eu and central asia regionally, at the level of foreign ministers. we have established regular human rights dialogues with all five countries. on energy, we are closer than ever to making our trans-caspian pipeline a reality, with the participation of turkmenistan in the southern energy gas corridor. in the sensitive area of water, we are now engaging in water policy dialogues to improve domestic water management polices, as has been done in eastern europe and the caucasus. on education, more central asian students than ever are coming to the eu and the eu is heavily involved with education sector reform in several countries. our technical assistance programme to support border management reform and combating drug trafficking remain among the leading international programmes in the region. as regards international financial institutions, the european bank for reconstruction and development continues to be a leading investor, to develop the private sector primarily, and we have expanded the mandate of the european investment bank to cover central asia, with a focus on energy and environment. we have managed to open new eu delegations in the region: in kyrgyzstan, tajikistan and uzbekistan, and hopefully also in turkmenistan in the not too distant future. the region more broadly continues to face difficult chapters and much remains to be done in terms of our relations with the region. the human rights situation is of general concern, as has been pointed out by ms alfano, and we need to see how best to make more of our engagements in this sensitive but very important area. as noted, we need to open delegations in all countries, which is important for increasing eu visibility and for promoting eu programmes, views and interests more efficiently. and given our admittedly limited financial resources for the region, the coordination of assistance with other international donors is crucial and has to be intensified continuously. the fact that our resources are limited has also made it increasingly important to focus our assistance, as the european parliament report rightly points out. this is already taking place with a limited amount of focal sectors per country. poverty alleviation remains a key objective and the poorest countries in the region – the kyrgyz republic and tajikistan – remain the primary beneficiaries of eu assistance. the region is diverse and, while we promote regional cooperation, notably on crucial issues such as water management, border management and drug trafficking, we have bilateral agendas with the five countries following their respective tracks, depending on individual needs and ambitions in terms of moving towards the eu and reform objectives. with kazakhstan for example, we just recently opened negotiations on an enhanced partnership and cooperation agreement, which will be a first for the region. let me conclude by saying that the european parliament has an important role to play as we move forward in our relations with central asia. we strongly welcome european parliament visits to the countries and regular interparliamentary dialogue and the increased parliamentary engagement that the report envisages. again we welcome parliament’s report which provides important input for our upcoming review and i congratulate the rapporteur.
the debate is closed. the vote will take place on thursday 15 december 2011 at 11.30. written declarations (rule 149) the president of the court of justice shall be informed of the decision of the court of first instance.
the next item is the report by mrs karima deli, on behalf of the committee on employment and social affairs, on health and safety at work (2011/2147 (ini)) (a7-0409/2011)
madam president, i would like to congratulate and thank karima delli for her excellent report. i had the pleasure and honour of being the socialist shadow rapporteur on this report and i feel it is my duty to remind the house of the result of the vote on this report in committee: 36 votes in favour, only 2 against. i think it's a very important element. i should also remind you that asbestos kills workers; to remind workers that musculoskeletal disorders are a problem; i'm reminded that stress drives workers to suicide. our defence in all of this is a new strategy for health and safety in the workplace from 2012 onwards. our weapon to defend ourselves in this whole situation is a new legislation, a new directive. and that, commissioner, is in your own hands, you have all the scientific evidence, you have all the documentation and you have - most importantly - the support of the european parliament to go ahead and ensure health and safety conditions for workers, especially in these difficult times of economic crisis that europe is going through.
member of the commission. − madam president, in february 2007 the commission adopted a communication entitled ‘improving quality and productivity at work: community strategy 2007-2012 on safety and health at work’. the strategy provided a political framework for improving occupational safety and health over the period 2007 to 2012 and laid out a road map for stakeholders to play an active role in achieving the objectives it identified. the fact that it was welcomed by all eu institutions highlights the importance of such an eu strategic framework for coordinating national policy and ensuring that workers enjoy safer and healthier conditions at work. in particular, this house adopted a resolution on 15 january 2008 calling on the commission to report to it on progress made at the half-way stage. in april this year the commission published a staff working paper entitled ‘mid-term review of the european strategy 2007-2012 on health and safety at work’. it takes stock of what has been achieved now that the strategy has reached the half-way mark, re-examines the policy orientations and sets out proposals for the future of eu policy on safety and health at work. the results of the mid-term review confirm that the strategy remains broadly fit for purpose, despite the changes that have taken place in the union since 2007, and in particular the impact of the financial and economic crisis. the strategy’s prime objective is achieving an ‘ongoing, sustainable and uniform reduction in accidents at work and occupational illnesses’. given the overall reduction in incidence in the period covered by the previous eu strategy, the strategy set an ambitious target to reduce the total incidence of accidents at work in the 27 member states by 25% from 2007 to 2012. a final estimate for the whole period covered by the strategy may not be available until 2014. this is because of time constraints related to collecting and processing national data by eurostat. the findings in the mid-term review show a general positive development involving a reduction in accidents at work over the period 2007 to 2009. but, despite this progress, there is still work to do under the current strategy. from the commission’s viewpoint, the assessment of the first part of the period covered by the strategy highlights a number of priorities. first, there is a need to simplify and update existing legislation and finalise proposals for legislation, after consulting the social partners and the stakeholders extensively. this relates in particular to the proposal for a revision of directive 2004/40/ec on electromagnetic fields (the commission proposal was adopted in june 2011 and is now being discussed by the co-legislators) and the proposal for a new directive on ergonomics to replace the existing manual handling and display screen equipment directives (the commission proposal may be adopted in the first half of 2012). furthermore, the commission will carry out an extensive screening of the implementation of all eu health and safety legislation, covering the period 2007 to 2012. the commission is required to present its final report on this in 2015 at the latest. second, we need to consolidate the encouraging results of the first phase of implementation and to take them further in terms of adopting and implementing national strategies for occupational safety and health. third, we need to build on experience with scoreboard 2009, with a view to developing a structured and commonly-accepted monitoring tool for evaluating future eu strategies for occupational safety and health. fourth, we need to carry out the final evaluation of the current strategy and, based on the findings, to identify the next steps in the health and safety area for the period after 2012. the commission welcomes the parliament’s decision to discuss and adopt a report on the mid-term review of the eu strategy on health and safety at work. i appreciate the ambitious nature of this document and share the house’s view of the importance of occupational safety and health policy, which is one of the most advanced areas of european social policy. the importance of health and safety at work does not diminish at a time of crisis and my recent visit to the bilbao agency for occupational health and safety was meant to signal this. in line with the europe 2020 strategy, improving working conditions goes naturally with job creation, promoting permanent employment and higher productivity, as the commission highlighted in its communication on ‘an agenda for new skills and jobs’. in 2012 the commission will complete the final evaluation of the current strategy and adopt a communication on eu occupational safety and health policy priorities for the post-2012 period based on the results of that evaluation. i can also add that i have started to work very closely with the danish presidency to keep health and safety among our priorities in the european union.

in writing. i voted in favour of the report, which sets out a comparative approach to eu and us practices in controlling financial support to afghanistan. the funds are normally managed through ngos, for-profit contractors, donors and direct financial support to the afghan government. however, as the structures in afghanistan are not comparable to those in developed countries, it is necessary to be aware that the afghan audit office is currently not independent from the afghan executive, and therefore does not meet international auditing standards. at the same time, there is limited freedom of access to internal audit reports, which calls into question the transparency of the procedures.
in writing. although i always vote in favour of using the globalisation fund, in this case i voted against. the request concerns the renault car company, in which the french state also holds shares. renault, despite the economic crisis, continues to make large profits but has for years been using money from the state and european budgets to carry out mass layoffs of workers. in this case, it wants to do the same for 3,000 workers, that is, not to secure from its own money and profits the necessary for the compulsory benefits and the 'social plan' which, according to french legislation, it must implement. as the french unions have also complained, renault has for years done nothing to protect workers' rights or to preserve jobs. finally, this issue seeks to take financial responsibility for the negative consequences of the reform of the pension system in france. but we cannot support that. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the social security scheme for the elderly, which is a new approach to social security.
in writing. the macroeconomic imbalance scoreboard is a key tool for the implementation of the economic governance legislative framework. for the united left, this economic governance package is the wrong answer to the crisis. it is not about coordinating economies, as it claims, but about imposing a permanent austerity pact on all workers throughout europe. as can be seen from the composition of this scoreboard, as it has been formulated, convergence is translated into an increase in competitiveness through the institutionalisation of austerity and the reduction of wages, pensions and benefits. indicators related to income inequality and poverty reduction are absent from the table, while the unemployment indicator has very little weight. the eurozone is facing huge structural problems which create imbalances and are particularly burdensome for workers in both surplus and deficit countries. as the economic governance package, and therefore the macroeconomic imbalance scoreboard, cannot offer fair and radical solutions for europe's exit from the crisis and the sustainability of its economic functioning, i voted against this motion for a resolution.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report, which is of great interest in view of the job insecurity in many eu member states due to the economic crisis and high unemployment rates. it is crucial to mention that member states should increase the staff and resources for labour inspection and achieve the target of one inspector per 10,000 workers, as recommended by the labour inspection organisation, which is currently not being met. at the same time, greater emphasis on mental health issues among workers is necessary to make them part of the process of identifying and preventing risks in their workplace.
